subject: [PATCH v3 11/12] mm/collapse: declare the collapse interface in collapse.h

2026-09-16.patch_summary: This patch declares the collapse interface in collapse.h, which includes functions and variables related to collapsing memory pages. The functions are: collapse_control_init, collapse_scan_pmd, collapse_run_pmd, and collapse_control_release. These functions are used for collapsing large pages into smaller ones. The patch also renames hugepage_vma_revalidate to collapse_vma_revalidate and adds comments to explain the order of function calls and lock usage. This is a preparation step for implementing MADV_COLLAPSE in madvise.c, but it does not introduce any functional changes.

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer David suggested replacing the current four functions (collapse_scan_pmd(), collapse_run_pmd(), etc.) with a single function called collapse_pmd() for cleaner code, but did not provide further details on how this would be implemented or what benefits it would bring.

Reviewer David requested removal of collapse_control_release() as it is not intended to release any resources, unless a previous patch updated its behavior.

Reviewer David (Arm) questioned the design of the collapse interface, specifically pointing out that collapse_vma_revalidate() is an odd part of it and suggesting the addition of a new function collapse_vma_validate() to perform initial validation on a given vma.

Reviewer David requested kerneldoc comments for the newly declared interface in collapse.h, suggesting that similar documentation should be added to other functions exposed by the same interface.
reviews.raw_body:
As discussed, having a single collapse_pmd() function might be cleaner if that's
easily possible.

	collapse_pmd()

---

And as discussed, I hope we can just get rid of a release function that's not
actually supposed to release anything right now (unless I was missing an update
in one of the patches).

---

Is it just me or is collapse_vma_revalidate() an odd part of this interface?

You'd expect a matching function that performs the initial validation on a given
vma.

Maybe we should have a

	orders = collapse_vma_validate(vma)

that really just wraps collapse_possible_orders(), an expose that instead to the
collapse users?

So they'd use collapse_vma_validate() to then call collapse_vma_revalidate()
after temporarily dropping the mmap lock?


[...]

---

Kerneldoc please. Applies to the other ones exposed as part of the same
interface as well.

-- 
Cheers,

David

2026-09-23.patch_summary: This patch declares the collapse interface in collapse.h, making it possible to use the functions from other files. The interface includes four main functions: collapse_control_init, collapse_scan_pmd, collapse_run_pmd, and collapse_control_release. These functions are used for collapsing memory pages and are part of a larger effort to implement MADV_COLLAPSE in madvise.c. The patch also renames hugepage_vma_revalidate to collapse_vma_revalidate and makes some minor changes to khugepaged.c.

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary:
Author addressed David's concern about the lack of a collapse_vma_validate() function by explaining that it would be redundant and unnecessary, given the existing checks in collapse_vma_revalidate().

Author agreed to add comments for each function in collapse.h, acknowledging that the current overview is insufficient and promising a fix.
reviews.raw_body:
collapse_vma_revalidate() re-checks what the scan ran under: a VMA at
the address, anonymous if the scan went that way, covering the PMD
range, allowing this order.

A collapse_vma_validate() could bundle what the callers check before a
scan, for the sake of symmetry. Feels like overkill to me.

---

Will do, for all of them. The overview in collapse.h stays; it is what
ties the calls together and says who holds the lock between them.

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov
